findings.title: docket-health now reads every _plans/*.md full-text on every Scan A run
findings.evidence: The shared board-scan python snippet gained a glob.glob('_plans/*.md') loop that opens and fully reads every plan file plus 3 re.search passes per file, every time docket-health prints. _plans/ is local-untracked and unbounded; on this checkout it is 21 files / 11MB, so each invocation reads ~11MB and regex-scans it (~100-300ms). Scan A runs in ac-loop Phase 0 (every run), the ac-human session/board opener, nightly reconcile, and weekly align — so this cost rides the most frequent read layer in the pipeline. The beadify-refusals population is in practice near zero; 11MB of IO is paid to compute it.
findings.fix: Prefilter before the regex passes: read only the head for status/polish markers (status: refined is frontmatter, top few lines), then read the full body only for files that pass. Or gate the whole loop on len(human-gate docket) > 0 / plan-gap|gate-incomplete being present — if the docket is empty the beadify-refusal count need not be recomputed.

findings.title: beadify-refusals regex triplet recompiles and rescans full plan text 3x per file
findings.evidence: Inside the loop each plan undergoes re.search('^status:', ...) then re.search('^polish_rounds:') then re.search('^polish_fixpoint_') then the needs-human alternating-Concat regex — four independent passes over ~500KB average file text where the first three target frontmatter (first ~1KB). The needs-human regex is the heaviest (lookbehind/lookahead alternation) and only runs on survivors, but the frontmatter probes scan the entire body each time; combined with the glob cost this is O(total-plan-bytes x 4) per run, ~1-2x the necessary work.
findings.fix: Read the frontmatter head slice (~2KB into _t) for the three ^key: probes, and run the heavy needs-human regex once over the full text only if the frontmatter probes pass; or use re.compile once outside the loop for all four patterns.
